description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

title.narrative: Output 1

description.narrative: 1.1. In order to improve taxpayer integrity and compliance, Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) approved the Inland Revenue (IR) Strategic Reform Plan (SRP) 2021-2025, which addresses the weaknesses identified in the Tax Administration Diagnostic Assessment Tool (TADAT) 2021, and implemented the following priority actions from the plan: (i) conducted and published the tax gap analysis for core taxes (Federal level Income Tax, Sales Tax, and Customs Duty); (ii) established a sectoral benchmark working committee, approved a benchmark study for inputs outputs, energy use, and value addition of the textile sector, and issued an office order to upgrade the automated system “FASTER” by incorporating benchmarks and input/output ratios to ensure certainty, transparency and truthfulness in processing of FBR sales tax refunds and issuance of valid and legitimate refunds to exporters; (iii) submitted for stakeholder consultations the approved draft amendments to the income tax, sales tax, sales tax on services in Islamabad Capital Territory, and federal excise duty that will harmonize and streamline core processes and procedures for tax administration. (iv) conducted and published findings of a specially designed independent third-party survey to monitor taxpayer perceptions regarding access to, and quality of, FBR products and services for the corporate sector (at least 10% of respondents are women-led companies).

title.narrative: Output 2

description.narrative: 1.2. To promote digital transformation and automation in tax administration, FBR implemented the following actions to introduce and operationalize the Synchronized Withholding Administration and Payment System (SWAPS)c: (i) established the legal framework to implement SWAPS through the National Assembly's approval of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Amendment); (ii) established the Directorate General of Digital Initiatives and began operationalization by deploying a Director General and four Deputy Directors; (iii) developed and approved an integrated application programming interface (API) that will enable synchronized withholding tax transactions and digital payments to multiple stakeholders in real-time and commenced engagement with Habib Bank, Bank Islami, and Bank Alfalah as model withholding agents for implementation of SWAPS; and (iv) approved and commenced implementation of an Information and Cybersecurity Governance Framework to upgrade its cyber security architecture.

title.narrative: Output 3

description.narrative: 1.3. To promote an inclusive and evidenced-based institutional framework for tax policy and administration, FBR: (i) established, through the parliamentary approval of Finance Act 2023, the Center for Tax Excellence to carry out data collection, including gender-disaggregated data, and independent tax research and analysis; and (ii) approved an evidence-based gender and social inclusion diagnostic study aligned with the 2022 National Gender Policy Framework and approved an action plan to implement its main recommendations.

title.narrative: Output 4

description.narrative: 2.1. To improve efficiency in cash management and ensure availability of cash when it is required, the Finance Division (FD) consolidates public monies held by autonomous bodies in the Treasury Single Account (TSA), in accordance with the Public Financial Management (PFM) Act 2019 (amended 2020). To this end, the FD: (i) approved the “Procedure for Recording and Reconciliation of Daily Receipt and Payment transactions”; (ii) published the list of autonomous bodies covered under the Cash Management and TSA Rules 2020 which consolidates public monies available; and (iii) launched pre-pilot of sweeping arrangements in FD bank accounts.

title.narrative: Output 5

description.narrative: 2.2. To minimize the accumulation of arrears and increase predictability in public expenditure, the FD approved with immediate effect operational guidelines related to annual and multi-annual commitment control framework which reconcile the availability of resources with commitments in accordance with the PFM Act 2019 (amended 2020).

title.narrative: Output 6

description.narrative: 2.3. To minimize deviations of fiscal outcomes from budget forecasts: (i) the Federal Government approved with immediate effect the functions of the Macro-Fiscal Policy Unit within the FD which includes the annual publication of an annual Fiscal Risk Statement (FRS) that presents a quantitative assessment of macroeconomic and fiscal risks and contingent liabilities stemming from state-owned enterprises, public-private partnerships, and natural disasters triggered by natural hazards and climate change; and (ii) FD published the annual FRS and disclosed it on their website to improve fiscal transparency and accountability.

title.narrative: Output 7

description.narrative: 2.4. The Federal Cabinet Secretariat approved rules assigning all debt management administrative functions to the Debt Management Office (DMO) following amendments to the Fiscal Responsibility and Debt Limitation Act, 2005 (FRDLA).

title.narrative: Output 8

description.narrative: 2.5. In order to strengthen gender and climate responsiveness of public financial systems: (i) starting in FY2023, the Federal Cabinet approved for submission to the National Assembly the year-end Government Performance Monitoring Reports for FY2022, incorporating achievements in gender and climate change responsive budget targets, in accordance with Section 35 of the PFM Act 2019; and (ii) the FD amended the Budget Call Circular FY2024 to make gender and climate change responsive budgeting mandatory and modify processes, instructions, and reporting templates to improve tracking and monitoring of gender and climate change budget allocations.

title.narrative: Output 9

description.narrative: 3.1. To promote domestic and foreign direct investment (FDI) in Pakistan, the Federal Cabinet has approved the Pakistan Investment Policy.

title.narrative: Output 10

description.narrative: 3.2. To promote a conducive business environment for FDI, FBR: (i) introduced a model tax treaty and tax treaty policy framework;e and (ii) rolled out a manual for exchange of information on request (EOIR) to the Offices of Inland Revenue, consistent with international tax transparency and cooperation standards.

title.narrative: Output 11

description.narrative: 3.3. National Assembly approved revisions to the tax laws needed to implement the Group of Twenty (G20) and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) base erosion and profit shifting (BEPS) measures for prevention of tax avoidance and evasion in cross-border transactions by: (i) increasing withholding tax rate on a “fee for offshore digital services” from 5% to 10%; (ii) rationalizing the scope of Pakistan's IT export regime to registered exporters duly certified by the Pakistan Software Export Board; (iii) prevention of tax treaty abuse through the introduction of beneficial owner concept and recharacterization of income and deduction with respect to permanent establishment; and (iv) making alternative dispute resolution mechanisms more effective.

title.narrative: Output 12

description.narrative: 3.4. To effectively implement the Pakistan Single Window (PSW) system: (i) PSW completed integration with four Other Government Agencies (OGAs) and operationalized PSW modules following the Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) signed between these OGAs and the PSW Company; (ii) PSW Governing Council approved a monitoring and evaluation (M&E) framework to strengthen monitoring and evaluation systems, processes, and practices, and guide future strategic decision-making.

title.narrative: Output 13

description.narrative: 3.5. To raise awareness and enhance access to information that will facilitate cross borders trade and investment, the PSW operationalized a Trade Information Portal which contains information on women-led businesses.

title.narrative: Output 14

description.narrative: 3.6. PSW approved and commenced implementation of its Gender Action Plan (GAP) 2022-2023 to promote and institutionalize gender equality considerations into its system.

title.narrative: Output 15

description.narrative: 3.7. To improve transparency and efficiency through digitization in the operations of the National Savings Scheme (NSS), the Central Directorate of National Savings (CDNS) completed the pilot phase of dematerialization of at least one saving product and has offered it to potential investors.

title.narrative: Output 16

description.narrative: 3.8. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (MOCC) published the updated Climate Change Policy for Pakistan on their website.

Action 1: To further improve taxpayer integrity and compliance: (i) FBR will implement risk-based operations based on findings from the tax gap analysis and sectoral benchmarks reports including improving the use of third-party data to systematically identify, quantify, and mitigate compliance risks, and establishing a structured compliance risk management program; (ii) Federal Cabinet will approve and submit to the National Assembly for approval the proposed amendments to the income tax, sales tax, sales tax on services in Islamabad Capital Territory, and federal excise duty to harmonize and streamline core processes and procedures for tax administration; and (iii) FBR will roll-out improved products and services for large companies such as simplification of the online process for filing tax forms. Target date: 2024-11-29

title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Nov 03, 2023 - Nov 29, 2024

description.narrative:
Policy 1: Tax administration and compliance improved Outcome 1: Tax revenue as a share of gross domestic product (GDP) improved to at least 12% of GDP (2022 baseline: 10.2% of GDP). Source: OECD Revenue Statistics in Asia and the Pacific.
Action 2: FBR to: (i) operationalize and roll-out SWAPS through integration in the banking sector; (ii) expand its pilot track and trace system (TTS) to cover at least one sector; (iii) establish and operationalize a control room for the TTS system in order to enhance tax revenue collections, reduce counterfeiting, and prevent smuggling of illicit goods; (iv) deploy upgraded software architecture for the Inland Revenue Information System (IRIS-2) to integrate modules for taxpayer declaration (income tax and sales tax), refund applications, withholding statements, and computerized payments; (v) align and operationalize the sales tax platform of IRIS-2 with the Web-Based Customs (WeBOC) System and Pakistan Single Window (PSW) System for real-time transfer and consolidation of sales transaction data; and (vi) roll-out modules under the IT Security Governance Risk and Compliance Policy Framework 2022-2024. Documentation Required: FBR notifications of (i) operationalization of the SWAPS in the banking sector, (ii) expansion of track and trace system to cover one additional sector, (iii) establishment and operationalization of the control room of the TTS, (iv) upgrade of the software architecture for IRIS-2, (v) alignment and operationalization of sales tax platform of IRIS-2 with the WeBOC systems, and (vi) rollout of modules under the IT Security Governance Risk and Compliance Policy Framework 2022-2024. Target date: 2024-11-29
Action 3: To promote an inclusive and evidenced-based institutional framework for tax policy and administration, FBR will: (i) fully operationalize the Center for Tax Excellence by recruiting and deploying adequately skilled staff (including at least one gender expert) according to approved organizational chart; and (ii) continue implementation of the Gender and Social Inclusion Policy to support the recruitment, promotion, and retention of women, transgender persons, persons living with disabilities, and minorities for inclusive and diversified workplace. Documentation Required: FBR notification of the (i) operationalization of CFRS, (ii) organizational chart of the CFRS with expert staff list, and (iii) implementation of the Gender and Social Inclusion Policy). Target date: 2024-11-29

title.narrative: Policy 3 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Oct 01, 2021 - Oct 31, 2021

description.narrative:
Policy 3: Mobilization of Domestic and Non-Debt Resources Improved NA
Action 2: To promote a conducive business environment for FDI, FBR: (i) introduced a model tax treaty and tax treaty policy framework;e and (ii) rolled out a manual for exchange of information on request (EOIR) to the Offices of Inland Revenue, consistent with international tax transparency and cooperation standards. Target date: 2021-10-31
Action 3: National Assembly approved revisions to the tax laws needed to implement the Group of Twenty (G20) and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) base erosion and profit shifting (BEPS) measures for prevention of tax avoidance and evasion in cross-border transactions by: (i) increasing withholding tax rate on a “fee for offshore digital services” from 5% to 10%; (ii) rationalizing the scope of Pakistan's IT export regime to registered exporters duly certified by the Pakistan Software Export Board; (iii) prevention of tax treaty abuse through the introduction of beneficial owner concept and recharacterization of income and deduction with respect to permanent establishment; and (iv) making alternative dispute resolution mechanisms more effective. Target date: 2021-10-31
Action 4: To effectively implement the Pakistan Single Window (PSW) system: (i) PSW completed integration with four Other Government Agencies (OGAs) and operationalized PSW modules following the Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) signed between these OGAs and the PSW Company; (ii) PSW Governing Council approved a monitoring and evaluation (M&E) framework to strengthen monitoring and evaluation systems, processes, and practices, and guide future strategic decision-making. Target date: 2021-10-31
Action 5: To raise awareness and enhance access to information that will facilitate cross borders trade and investment, the PSW operationalized a Trade Information Portal which contains information on women-led businesses. Target date: 2021-10-31
Action 6: PSW approved and commenced implementation of its Gender Action Plan (GAP) 2022-2023 to promote and institutionalize gender equality considerations into its system. Target date: 2021-10-31
Action 7: To improve transparency and efficiency through digitization in the operations of the National Savings Scheme (NSS), the Central Directorate of National Savings (CDNS) completed the pilot phase of dematerialization of at least one saving product and has offered it to potential investors. Target date: 2021-10-31
Action 8: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (MOCC) published the updated Climate Change Policy for Pakistan on their website. Target date: 2021-10-31
Action 1: To further formalize domestic and FDI promotion in Pakistan, the Federal Cabinet will approve and submit the proposed National Investment Bill to the National Assembly.
